control.decode: 128 tokens in 9.21 s = 13.78 tok/s (97.7% VRAM expert hits)

tp.loader: p6.2 tp seam: 64 sliced weight copies (= 10 layers x 6 seam slices + 2 layers x 2 DEAD indexer-attn_q_b slices, never read by any graph)
tp.decode: 128 tokens in 9.18 s = 13.83 tok/s (97.7% VRAM expert hits, expert counters identical to control)

findings.numerics: control and tp emitted IDENTICAL 128/128 greedy tokens (first difference: none). The f32 reduce-order change flipped ZERO knife-edge argmaxes through 8 chunked-prefill passes + 128 decode steps. Within the P6 section-4 calibration rule (f32 induced error host-bounded ~1e-4, p6_tp_algebra); no bit-identity CLAIMED beyond this prompt - the engine's cross-process reproducibility distribution applies.
findings.decode_overhead: 13.78 vs 13.83 tok/s = +0.4% with 10/40 layers sharded - the seam (2 extra FA launches, 2 sliced mul_mats, 1 add, per sharded layer) is invisible at n=1, as expected for launch-bound decode inside cached graphs.
findings.prefill_overhead: 27.2 vs 20.2 tok/s = 25.7% SLOWER with only 10 of 40 layers sharded. Linear extrapolation to 40/40 (~103%) would exceed the kill gate (10%) and outrun the ~1.8x halving the cross-card plan prices - but the spike's implementation is NOT yet exonerated: candidates include ggml-cuda kernel-path choices for the 4096-wide sliced mul_mats or the two half-head FA calls, none of which exist on a real split (each card runs ONE half-k GEMM and ONE half-head FA). The verdict is HELD until the attribution run separates seam algebra from spike plumbing.
findings.runner_guard_fired_correctly: the anti-no-op guard refused the comparison because its expected-slice formula (3/layer) was wrong (6/layer + 2 dead indexer slices); the engine lines showed the seam WAS built. Fixed with this receipt: formula 6/layer, loader now refuses to slice indexer.attn_q_b (suffix collision, dead copies).

next: attribution window: control vs --tp-layers 0 (1 layer, slope check) vs the NO-FA-variant at 10 layers (single full FA, only the o-projection GEMM reduced - isolates FA-split cost from GEMM-path cost) - same runner. NO-GO or GO applies only after that run; no cross-card claim in either direction before it.
limitations: one prompt, one greedy temperature-0 pass; tokens prove composition (reduce node rides the hc machine and the per-column carry) on THAT trajectory only; the dead indexer slices added a few MB of never-read VRAM to the tp run (too small to explain 25.7%, but they are removed for the attribution run); prompt rate measured on 512 tokens / 8 chunk passes - no separate n=64 single-pass timing yet.
